subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How are root hair cells adapted for absorbing water?
options: They have a large surface area to absorb water and minerals
questions.explain: Root hair cells have a long projection giving a large surface area for absorbing water and mineral ions.

questions.q: Which mineral-carrying tissue is also important in supporting the plant?
questions.explain: Lignified xylem vessels help support the plant as well as transporting water.

questions.q: How does mineral ion uptake by root hair cells usually occur?
options: By active transport against the concentration gradient
questions.explain: Mineral ions are taken into roots by active transport, which requires energy from respiration.

questions.q: Which tissue transports water and mineral ions up the plant?
questions.explain: Xylem carries water and dissolved minerals upwards from the roots.

questions.q: In which direction(s) can phloem transport substances?
options: Both up and down the plant
questions.explain: Translocation in phloem can move dissolved food in both directions to where it is needed.

questions.q: Which feature distinguishes phloem from xylem?
options: Phloem is made of living cells
Phloem is made of dead cells
questions.explain: Phloem is composed of living cells, unlike the dead xylem vessels.

questions.q: What is the 'transpiration stream'?
options: The continuous movement of water from roots up through the xylem to the leaves
Water draining out of the soil
The movement of air through stomata
The flow of sugars in phloem
questions.explain: As water evaporates from leaves, more is pulled up through the xylem in the transpiration stream.

questions.q: What is transpiration?
options: The movement of sugars in phloem
The loss of water vapour from the leaves of a plant
questions.explain: Transpiration is the evaporation and loss of water vapour, mainly through the stomata of leaves.

questions.q: What does phloem transport?
questions.explain: Phloem transports dissolved food (sucrose) in the process of translocation.

questions.q: Which mineral ion is needed to make chlorophyll and is absorbed by the roots?
questions.explain: Magnesium ions are needed to make chlorophyll for photosynthesis.

questions.q: Through which structures do most plants lose water vapour from their leaves?
questions.explain: Most water vapour is lost through the stomata on the leaf surface.

questions.q: Which condition would slow the rate of transpiration?
questions.explain: High humidity reduces the concentration gradient of water vapour, slowing transpiration.

questions.q: Which change would increase the rate of transpiration?
questions.explain: Moving air carries away water vapour, keeping a steep gradient and increasing transpiration.

questions.q: Translocation in the phloem requires energy because it is...
options: an active process moving dissolved food to where it is needed
questions.explain: Translocation is an active process that moves dissolved sugars around the plant.

questions.q: Which piece of apparatus is used to estimate the rate of water uptake by a shoot?
questions.explain: A potometer measures water uptake, used to investigate transpiration rate.

questions.q: A plant in dry, windy conditions wilts because...
options: water is lost faster than the roots can replace it
questions.explain: High transpiration in dry, windy air can lose water faster than roots absorb it, causing wilting.

questions.q: What is the main force that pulls water up through the xylem?
options: Evaporation of water from the leaves (transpiration pull)
questions.explain: Water evaporating from leaves creates a pull that draws water up the xylem.

questions.q: Why does transpiration slow down when stomata close at night?
options: Water vapour can no longer escape easily through the closed pores
questions.explain: With stomata closed, water vapour cannot diffuse out, so transpiration slows.

questions.q: Why does increased light intensity tend to increase transpiration?
options: Stomata open in the light for photosynthesis, allowing more water to escape
questions.explain: In light, stomata open to allow gas exchange for photosynthesis, so more water vapour is lost.

questions.q: Why does increasing temperature usually increase transpiration?
options: Water molecules evaporate and diffuse faster
questions.explain: Higher temperatures speed up evaporation and diffusion of water vapour from the leaf.

questions.q: Where does most water loss from a plant occur?
options: Through the stomata in the leaves
questions.explain: Most water is lost as vapour through the stomata in the leaves.

questions.q: Why are xylem vessels strengthened with lignin?
options: To keep them hollow and support the plant
questions.explain: Lignin strengthens xylem vessels, keeping them open and helping support the plant.
